test_cases.test_name: Functional Test: Chart Creation and Nelson Rules Application
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully create X-bar/R and p-charts from a CSV file and correctly apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules to identify out-of-control points.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
Valid CSV test file with sample QC data is available
User account with chart creation permissions is configured

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured user credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and the main dashboard interface is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the main dashboard screen

test_steps.action: Navigate to the chart creation module and select the option to import data from a CSV file.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays a file browser dialog for selecting a CSV file.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the file import dialog

test_steps.action: Select the provided test CSV file containing sample QC data and confirm the import.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes the file and displays a preview of the data without errors.
data_to_capture: Any error messages generated during import

test_steps.action: Configure the chart settings to generate an X-bar/R chart using the imported data columns.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates and displays the X-bar/R chart with calculated control limits.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the generated X-bar/R chart

test_steps.action: Enable the vendor's standard Nelson rules from the chart analysis options.
test_steps.expected_result: The system applies Nelson rules and visually highlights any out-of-control points on the chart.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the chart with Nelson rules applied
List of any flagged out-of-control points

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 4 and 5 to create and analyze a p-chart with the same dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully generates a p-chart and applies Nelson rules correctly.
data_to_capture: List of any flagged out-of-control points on the p-chart

acceptance_criteria: X-bar/R and p-charts are generated without system errors
Nelson rules are applied and correctly flag known out-of-control data points
Chart visualizations match the expected output based on the test data
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GMP requirements for data integrity in QC processes
data_integrity_requirements: Imported data must remain unaltered during chart creation
Nelson rule calculations must be accurate and reproducible
Chart configurations must be saved as controlled records

test_cases.test_name: Performance Test: Data Loading and Chart Rendering Speed
test_cases.objective: To validate that the SPC dashboard meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering charts within specified time limits under supported hardware configurations.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard is installed on vendor-supported hardware
Test CSV file with 100,000 data points is prepared
System monitoring tool is available to measure performance

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard and navigate to the data import function.
test_steps.expected_result: Dashboard is accessible and ready for data import.
data_to_capture: System time at start of test
Available system memory and CPU usage

test_steps.action: Initiate import of the test CSV file containing 100,000 data points and start a timer.
test_steps.expected_result: System begins processing the file import without freezing or crashing.

test_steps.action: Stop the timer when the data import is complete and the system indicates readiness for chart creation.
test_steps.expected_result: Data import completes successfully and system displays confirmation.
data_to_capture: Total elapsed time for data loading

test_steps.action: Configure an X-bar/R chart using the imported dataset and start a timer when initiating chart generation.
test_steps.expected_result: System begins processing the chart rendering request.
data_to_capture: Time stamp when chart generation begins

test_steps.action: Stop the timer when the chart is fully rendered and interactive on the screen.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart is completely displayed with all data points and control limits visible.
data_to_capture: Time stamp when chart rendering completes
Total elapsed time for chart rendering

test_steps.action: Apply a filter to the chart data (e.g., date range filter) and measure the time to re-render the chart.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart updates to reflect the filtered data without requiring full reload.
data_to_capture: Time required for filter application and re-rendering

acceptance_criteria: 100,000 data points load in less than 5 seconds
Charts render completely in less than 2 seconds after configuration
Filter changes result in chart updates in less than 2 seconds
System remains stable and responsive throughout performance testing
regulatory_basis: FDA guidance on computerized systems in pharmaceutical manufacturing
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be accurately represented in charts regardless of loading speed
No data corruption or loss during high-volume operations
Chart calculations must remain accurate under performance load

test_cases.objective: To verify that the dashboard correctly restricts data views and functionality based on assigned user roles as per the vendor's standard implementation.
prerequisites: User accounts with different roles (e.g., Viewer, Analyst, Admin) are created
System is installed and accessible
Sample datasets are loaded

test_steps.action: Log in to the SPC dashboard with a user account assigned a 'Viewer' role.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful. The user interface displays only view-only options for charts and reports.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the user interface after login

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a chart configuration or annotation on a released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents any modifications and displays a message indicating insufficient permissions.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in with an 'Admin' role account.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful. The user interface displays full administrative options, including configuration and user management.

acceptance_criteria: User access is correctly restricted based on assigned roles
Released datasets are read-only for non-admin users as required
No unauthorized access to configuration changes is permitted
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Limited access to authorized individuals
URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets
data_integrity_requirements: User permissions must enforce data integrity by preventing unauthorized alterations to controlled records and configurations.

test_cases.test_name: Data Import and Chart Rendering Performance
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering control charts within specified time limits.
prerequisites: System is installed on supported hardware
A test CSV file containing at least 100,000 data points is prepared
Stopwatch or system timer is available

test_steps.action: Initiate the data import function and select the prepared CSV file with 100k data points. Start the timer.
test_steps.expected_result: The system begins importing the data and displays a progress indicator.

test_steps.action: Stop the timer once the import is complete and the data is displayed in the system.
test_steps.expected_result: The data import completes successfully in less than 5 seconds.

test_steps.action: Apply a filter to the imported dataset (e.g., filter by a specific date range) and start the timer.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes the filter change and begins re-rendering the chart.
data_to_capture: Time taken for chart to fully render after filter application

test_steps.action: Stop the timer once the chart is fully rendered and interactive.
test_steps.expected_result: The chart is rendered in less than 2 seconds after the filter change.

acceptance_criteria: Data import of 100k points completes in under 5 seconds
Chart re-rendering after filter changes completes in under 2 seconds
System remains stable and responsive during high-load operations
regulatory_basis: General GAMP principle for ensuring system performance meets user needs
URS-020-010: Load 100k data points in < 5 seconds
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes
data_integrity_requirements: Performance must be adequate to ensure data is processed correctly and completely without timeouts or corruption.

test_cases.test_name: Performance Test: Large Dataset Loading and Chart Rendering
test_cases.objective: Verify the system meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering charts within specified timeframes under supported hardware conditions.
prerequisites: System installed on supported hardware
Test dataset with 100k data points available
User with appropriate permissions logged in

test_steps.action: Navigate to data import section and select the 100k data point CSV file for upload
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the file and begins processing the data import
data_to_capture: Time from file selection completion to data loading completion

test_steps.action: Apply filter changes to the loaded dataset and initiate chart rendering
test_steps.expected_result: Charts render successfully with updated filters applied
data_to_capture: Time from filter application to complete chart rendering

acceptance_criteria: 100k data points load in less than 5 seconds
Charts render in less than 2 seconds after filter changes
No performance degradation or system crashes during testing
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for system performance reliability
GAMP 5 for performance verification of commercial software
data_integrity_requirements: Performance metrics must be accurately captured and documented
Test data integrity maintained throughout performance testing

test_cases.test_name: Integration Test: ODBC Data Import and AD Authentication
test_cases.objective: Verify successful integration with external data sources via ODBC connections and Active Directory authentication if supported by vendor.
prerequisites: ODBC data source configured and accessible
Active Directory environment available if supported
Test user credentials available for both systems

test_steps.action: Configure ODBC connection settings in the SPC dashboard using standard vendor connectors
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully connects to the ODBC data source without errors

test_steps.action: Import data from the ODBC source and create a control chart using the imported data
test_steps.expected_result: Data imports successfully and charts render correctly with ODBC-sourced data

test_steps.action: If supported, configure Active Directory integration and attempt login with AD credentials
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully authenticates user via Active Directory integration

acceptance_criteria: ODBC data import completes successfully without data loss
Charts render correctly with ODBC-sourced data
AD authentication works correctly if supported by vendor
All integration features function as specified in vendor documentation
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and data integrity
GAMP 5 for integration testing of commercial software components
data_integrity_requirements: Data integrity maintained during ODBC transfer process
Authentication credentials handled securely
Accurate data mapping between systems

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system's vendor scheduler correctly generates and emails reports according to a predefined schedule.
prerequisites: System is installed and operational
Valid user account with scheduling permissions
Configured email server settings in the system
Valid email recipient address for testing
A saved chart configuration

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard with a user account that has scheduling permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and gains access to the scheduling features.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the report scheduling module and create a new scheduled task for a PDF report.
test_steps.expected_result: Scheduler interface loads, allowing creation of a new task with options for report type, frequency, and recipients.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the scheduler configuration screen

test_steps.action: Configure the task to run immediately (or on a short, testable interval) and select the pre-saved chart configuration and PDF format.
test_steps.expected_result: Task is configured with all required parameters set correctly.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the completed task configuration

test_steps.action: Save the scheduled task and verify it appears in the active tasks list.
test_steps.expected_result: Task is saved successfully and is visible in the list of scheduled jobs with a status of 'Active' or 'Pending'.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the task list showing the new job

test_steps.action: Wait for the scheduled time to elapse and check the specified email inbox for the report.
test_steps.expected_result: An email is received containing the PDF report attachment generated from the selected chart configuration.
data_to_capture: Confirmation that PDF is attached and uncorrupted

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates a PDF report based on the scheduled task.
The generated report is emailed to the specified recipient without errors.
The content of the emailed report matches the selected chart configuration.
regulatory_basis: URS-020-006: The system shall support scheduled report emails using vendor scheduler.
data_integrity_requirements: The report data must be an accurate representation of the source chart configuration.
The scheduling configuration must be retained as a controlled record per URS-020-008.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can successfully authenticate users via Active Directory if the vendor supports this feature.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured for AD integration (if supported)
Access to a test Active Directory domain
Valid AD user credentials for testing
Network connectivity to the AD server

test_steps.action: Attempt to launch the SPC dashboard login page from a client machine on the domain.
test_steps.expected_result: Login page loads, displaying fields for username and password.

test_steps.action: Enter valid Active Directory credentials (domain\username and password) into the login fields.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the credentials and processes the login request.

test_steps.action: Submit the login credentials and observe the system response.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully authenticated and granted access to the dashboard according to their AD role.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the main dashboard after login
User role/permissions displayed in the system

test_steps.action: Verify the user's role-based view access matches the permissions defined in Active Directory groups.
test_steps.expected_result: The dashboard menus and features available correspond to the user's AD group memberships.
data_to_capture: List of accessible features vs. restricted features

test_steps.action: Log out of the system and attempt to log in with invalid AD credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: System rejects the login attempt with an appropriate error message and does not grant access.

acceptance_criteria: Users with valid AD credentials can successfully log into the system.
User permissions and role-based views are correctly mapped from AD groups.
Invalid AD credentials are rejected by the system.
regulatory_basis: URS-020-013: Integrate with AD for user authentication if supported by vendor.
URS-020-004: The dashboard shall allow role-based view access.
data_integrity_requirements: Authentication must be secure to prevent unauthorized access to QC data.
Role mappings must be accurate to ensure data is accessed appropriately.

test_cases.test_name: ODBC Data Source Integration and Import Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully connect to and import data from a configured ODBC data source using the vendor's standard connectors.
prerequisites: OQ-001 (Installation Verification) completed
A test database with a known schema and sample QC data is available
ODBC data source is configured on the test machine
Valid user credentials for the database

test_steps.action: Launch the SPC dashboard and navigate to the data import section.
test_steps.expected_result: Dashboard opens successfully, and the data import interface is accessible.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the data import interface

test_steps.action: Select the option to import data via an ODBC connection from the available import methods.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays a configuration dialog for specifying ODBC connection parameters.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the ODBC connection dialog

test_steps.action: Enter the pre-configured ODBC Data Source Name (DSN), and valid authentication credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the credentials and establishes a connection to the database.

test_steps.action: Select a predefined table or view from the database containing sample QC data and map the columns to the required SPC chart fields.
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully retrieves the database schema and allows for column mapping.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the column mapping screen

test_steps.action: Initiate the data import process and confirm the import.
test_steps.expected_result: System imports the data without errors and displays a success message with the record count.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the chart creation module and attempt to create an X-bar/R chart using the imported ODBC data.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart is rendered successfully using the data from the ODBC source.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the generated X-bar/R chart

acceptance_criteria: ODBC connection is established successfully without errors.
Data is imported completely and accurately from the source database.
Imported data can be used to create a standard SPC chart (X-bar/R).
The number of records imported matches the expected count from the source.
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records integrity when importing data from external systems.
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that data imported via ODBC is an exact representation of the source data.
Confirm that the import process is logged or traceable.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard correctly integrates with the organization's Active Directory for user authentication and role-based access, if supported by the vendor.
prerequisites: OQ-001 (Installation Verification) completed
SPC dashboard is configured for AD integration (if supported)
Test accounts exist in AD with different roles (e.g., Viewer, Analyst)
Network connectivity to the AD server is confirmed

test_steps.action: Attempt to launch the SPC dashboard application.
test_steps.expected_result: System presents a login prompt or redirects to an enterprise authentication page.

test_steps.action: Enter the credentials for a test user account that exists in Active Directory but is not configured in the SPC dashboard.
test_steps.expected_result: If AD integration is supported, login is denied. If not supported, the test is concluded as 'Not Applicable'.

test_steps.action: Enter the credentials for a valid test 'Viewer' role account from Active Directory.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully authenticated and logged into the dashboard with read-only permissions.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the user interface showing limited permissions

test_steps.action: While logged in as the 'Viewer', attempt to perform a restricted action (e.g., modifying a chart configuration or deleting data).
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents the action and may display an 'access denied' message, consistent with role-based view access.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the access denied message or disabled controls

test_steps.action: Log out and repeat the login process with a test 'Analyst' or higher-privilege AD account.
test_steps.expected_result: User is authenticated and granted appropriate permissions for data creation and modification.

acceptance_criteria: If AD integration is a vendor-supported feature, authentication succeeds only with valid AD credentials.
Role-based permissions defined in the system are correctly applied based on the user's AD group membership.
Users without valid AD credentials (or if unsupported) cannot access the system.
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for secure, role-based access controls and user authentication.
data_integrity_requirements: Authentication system must ensure only authorized personnel can access and modify data and configurations.
